sections.sectionTitle: Section A: Introduction to Animal Husbandry

topics.title: Meaning, scope and importance of animal husbandry

subtopics.content: a. Meaning, scope and importance of animal husbandry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the meaning (rearing of farm animals), scope (nutrition, health, etc.) and importance (source of food, employment, income, etc.) of farm animals

subtopics.content: a. Problems in animal production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know and understand the problems in animal production in West Africa and possible solutions

topics.title: Quality and safety standard of animal food products

subtopics.content: a. Quality and safety standard of animal food products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe quality and safety standards, practices for maintaining standards, effects of consuming poor animal products and roles of agencies involved in animal food product safety and quality

subtopics.content: a. Classification based on digestive system: ruminants e.g. sheep, goat, cattle; non-ruminants (monogastrics) e.g. poultry, pigs; non-ruminant herbivores e.g. rabbits, grasscutter, guinea pigs
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify farm animals based on digestive system

subtopics.content: b. Concept of traditional (cattle, sheep, goat) and non-traditional farm animals (rabbit, grasscutter, snails)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to distinguish traditional from non-traditional farm animals

sections.sectionTitle: Section B: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals

topics.title: Meaning of anatomy, physiology and the external orientation of farm animals

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of the terms: anatomy, physiology and the external orientation of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the terms anatomy and physiology and know the parts and positions of external parts (orientation) of farm animals e.g. the head of the cow is anterior to the hind limb or udder

subtopics.content: a. Comparative anatomy of digestive system of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the main features of the digestive systems of ruminants, non-ruminant herbivores and monogastrics and the differences in structure and functions

subtopics.content: b. Digestion and absorption processes in the various classes of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand digestion processes, the role of specific enzymes in digestion of carbohydrates, proteins, fats and oils, and the structures and processes involved in absorption of nutrients

subtopics.content: a. Parts of the Central Nervous System (CNS) and Autonomic Nervous System (ANS)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the parts of the CNS and ANS and describe their mode of action

subtopics.content: b. Functions of the ANS
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the functions of the ANS, explain how nerve impulses are transmitted and how homeostasis is ensured

subtopics.content: c. Endocrine system: (i) endocrine glands and their functions; (ii) hormones and their functions
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know what endocrine glands are, their location and functions; hormones, their functions and mode of action, and the need to administer synthetic hormones

subtopics.content: a. Integumentary, skeletal and muscular systems
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the structure and functions of the integumentary (skin), skeletal and muscular systems

subtopics.content: a. Anatomy of the reproductive system of poultry and livestock
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand reproductive terms e.g. puberty, oestrous cycle, oestrus/anoestrus, ovulation, fertilization, libido, and know the main features of the reproductive system of poultry and livestock

subtopics.content: b. Functions of organs and parts of the reproductive system
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the functions of the organs and parts of the reproductive system

subtopics.content: c. Reproductive processes
subtopics.objective: Candidates should describe the stages from puberty through mating to parturition, differences between poultry and livestock, and know reproductive hormones and their functions

subtopics.content: a. Structure and functions
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the organs (heart, blood vessels), tissues (blood, lymph) and cells (blood cells) and their functions, and differences between pulmonary and systemic circulation

subtopics.content: b. Heart and pulse rate
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the meaning of heart and pulse rate and interpret their values

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance of respiration
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the term respiration and its importance

subtopics.content: b. Structure and functions of the respiratory system
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the structure and functions of the parts of the respiratory system of livestock

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance of excretion
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the term excretion and its importance

subtopics.content: b. Structure and functions of the excretory system
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the structure and functions of the parts of the excretory system of livestock

subtopics.content: c. Excretory products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should give examples of excretory products and how they are eliminated from the body

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the term nutrition, its role in animal production (e.g. improves body resistance, production level) and basic terms such as nutrients, diet, ration, roughages, malnutrition, concentrates

subtopics.content: b. Modes of feeding
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the differences in modes of feeding in non-ruminant herbivores, ruminants, carnivores and omnivores, and the influence of dentition on mode of feeding

subtopics.content: a. Types, composition and functions of the feed nutrients
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know feedstuffs and supplements, their main composition and the functions of the major nutrients

subtopics.content: b. Classification of feedstuffs
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to group feedstuffs according to the major nutrients they supply

subtopics.content: c. Food tests
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to use simple food tests to detect carbohydrates, fats and oils, and proteins in feedstuffs

subtopics.content: d. Producers and suppliers of feedstuffs and supplements
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know major producers and suppliers of feedstuffs in the country

topics.title: Formulation and preparation of animal feeds

subtopics.content: a. Common terms used in feed formulation
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand terms such as dry matter, diet, metabolizable energy, malnutrition

subtopics.content: b. Factors considered in the formulation of ration
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know factors such as age, physiological state of the animal and cost of feed ingredients

subtopics.content: c. Steps in the formulation of ration
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to use the Pearson Square Method to formulate a balanced ration

topics.title: Handling and storage of animal feeds

subtopics.content: a. Importance of feed storage and features of storage structures
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the importance of feed storage and features of storage structures/containers

subtopics.content: b. Factors that affect the quality of stored feed
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know factors such as storage/ambient temperature, humidity, water content, pests and rodents, and follow practices in handling stored feed e.g. drying, fumigation

topics.title: Record keeping and estimation of cost of prepared feed

subtopics.content: a. Record keeping and estimation of cost of prepared feed
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to keep feed records and estimate the cost of prepared feed

topics.title: Pests of stored feed and their control

subtopics.content: a. Pests of stored feed and their control
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify common pests of stored feeds, their effects (damage, contamination), and preventive and control measures

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of terms
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the terms disease, pest and parasite

subtopics.content: a. Signs of good and ill-health
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the characteristics of healthy and sick animals and describe the signs and symptoms of disease in farm animals

topics.title: Factors that predispose animals to diseases

subtopics.content: a. Factors that predispose animals to diseases
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand how factors such as overcrowding, poor nutrition and poor housing predispose animals to diseases, and know causes of stress and measures to reduce stress

topics.title: Effects of diseases, pests and parasites on animal production

subtopics.content: a. Effects of diseases, pests and parasites on animal production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the effects on economic value of animals/products and income e.g. reduced value/output, loss of income, reduced quality of products

topics.title: Zoonotic diseases; their importance and prevention

subtopics.content: a. Zoonotic diseases; their importance and prevention
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the term zoonotic disease and its importance e.g. effect on human health and preventive methods

subtopics.content: a. Classification of pathogens
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the classes of pathogens (viruses, bacteria, fungi and protozoa)

subtopics.content: b. Pathogenic diseases and their economic importance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know common pathogenic diseases and their economic importance in animal production

subtopics.content: c. Principles for prevention and control of diseases of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know principles (e.g. nutrition, vaccination) with respect to cost, suitability and efficiency, and use prophylactics (coccidiostat, antibiotics, anti-stress drugs, vitamins)

subtopics.content: d. Management practices in the prevention and control of diseases of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know practices such as deworming, dipping, dusting, treatment of wounds and sores, spraying and fumigation of animal houses, drug administration and precautions in the use of drugs

subtopics.content: a. Types and examples of parasites
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the two main types of parasites (ecto and endoparasites) and examples

subtopics.content: b. Structure, life cycle and mode of feeding
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the structure, life cycle and mode of feeding of common endo- and ectoparasites

subtopics.content: c. Conditions that influence parasite population
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know conditions that affect parasite population and how they could be changed to reduce it

subtopics.content: a. Prevention and control of parasites
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know measures such as deworming, drenching, dipping, farm sanitation, and the use of appropriate equipment and chemicals

subtopics.content: a. Economic importance of parasites
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the economic importance of ecto- and endoparasites (i) on the host e.g. ectoparasites damage skin and hides, suck blood; endoparasites damage internal organs; (ii) on animal products e.g. loss of income, increased expenditure due to control measures

sections.sectionTitle: Section E: Genetic Principles and Animal Improvement

topics.title: Heredity, basic genetic terms and Mendel's first law of inheritance

subtopics.content: a. Heredity, basic genetic terms and Mendel's first law of inheritance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand heredity and genetic terms (e.g. gene, genotype, phenotype, sex-linkage), cell division (meiosis and mitosis), inheritance of traits and Mendel's first law

topics.title: Meaning, objectives and benefits of animal improvement

subtopics.content: a. Meaning, objectives and benefits of animal improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand animal improvement and know its objectives and benefits e.g. disease resistance, better growth rate

topics.title: Performance traits of improved and unimproved animals

subtopics.content: a. Performance traits of improved and unimproved animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to analyze data to determine superiority of improved animals based on genotype and phenotype

topics.title: Methods of animal improvement; advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.content: a. Methods of animal improvement; advantages and disadvantages
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know methods (introduction, selection, breeding), types of breeding (e.g. cross breeding, line breeding) and their advantages and disadvantages

topics.title: Nutritional and environmental factors affecting animal improvement

subtopics.content: a. Nutritional and environmental factors affecting animal improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the nutritional and environmental factors that affect animal improvement

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and process of artificial insemination (A.I.)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the term A.I., describe the technique and name tools and equipment used

subtopics.content: b. Advantages of A.I.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the advantages of A.I.

subtopics.content: c. Signs of heat (oestrus) and handling procedures in the collection and storage of semen
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to detect heat through signs of heat and know proper handling in collection and storage of semen

sections.sectionTitle: Section F: Introduction to Environmental Physiology

topics.title: Internal and external environment of animals

subtopics.content: a. Internal and external environment of animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know what constitutes the internal environment (e.g. blood glucose level, body temperature) and external environment (e.g. ambient temperature, humidity, wind) and examples of acceptable levels

topics.title: The role of the nervous and endocrine systems in homeostasis and animal's response to stimuli

subtopics.content: a. The role of the nervous and endocrine systems in homeostasis and animal's response to stimuli
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the role of these systems in environmental awareness, responses to stimuli and maintenance of homeostasis e.g. normal levels of body temperature, respiration and heart rate

topics.title: Determination of room temperature, body temperature and respiration rate in farm animals

subtopics.content: a. Determination of room temperature, body temperature and respiration rate in farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know physiological and behavioural responses to heat, cold, exercise, and be able to use equipment for measuring temperature, humidity, respiration rate and heart beat, and interpret the data

topics.title: Effects of climate on farm animals

subtopics.content: a. Effects of climate on farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know indirect and direct effects of climate (e.g. disease prevalence, feed quality and quantity, heat stress, increased abortion) and understand thermo-neutral zone and optimum temperature in relation to productivity

topics.title: Modification of animal environment and management practices to reduce stress on animals

subtopics.content: a. Modification of animal environment and management practices to reduce stress on animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know ways of modifying the environment (housing, shading, cooling) and management (better feeding, time of grazing), and stress-minimizing strategies e.g. house design and lay-out, cool water, modified feeds, proper timing of drug administration

sections.sectionTitle: Section G: Monogastric and Domestic Pet Production

subtopics.content: a. Definition and characteristics of poultry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the term poultry and know its characteristics e.g. possession of beaks, wings, feathers

subtopics.content: b. Classes of poultry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the types of poultry e.g. chicken, turkey, ducks, guinea fowls and ostriches

subtopics.content: c. Breeds and types of poultry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know breeds: chicken e.g. Rhode Island Red, Plymouth Rock; guinea fowl e.g. Grey, Red-wattled (Pearl variety); turkey e.g. Broad Breasted Bronze; ducks e.g. Muscovy, Khaki Campbell; ostriches e.g. Blue Neck, Red Neck

subtopics.content: d. Importance/role of poultry production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the importance of producing the various types of poultry

subtopics.content: e. Systems of poultry production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the extensive, intensive and semi-intensive systems and their advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.content: f. Incubation and hatchery practices: (i) terminologies; (ii) natural and artificial incubation; (iii) selection of eggs for hatching; (iv) conditions necessary for hatching of eggs; (v) incubation process; (vi) candling of eggs; (vii) marketing of day-old chicks
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand terms such as fertile egg, hatchability, incubation and broodiness; differentiate natural and artificial incubation; select eggs for hatching; know incubation periods and conditions; describe the incubation process and hatchery practices (fumigation, temperature); understand candling; and know techniques and precautions for marketing day-old chicks

subtopics.content: g. Management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know housing, breeding, brooding, feeding, sanitation, pest and disease control, identification and record keeping

subtopics.content: h. Processing and marketing of poultry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know slaughtering and processing, quality control, packaging, preservation and storage, marketing outlets, transportation and advertisement

subtopics.content: i. Prospects of producing the various types of poultry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know prospects, consumer preferences, market availability and cost

subtopics.content: a. Types, breeds and characteristics
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know types of pig (bacon, lard and pork types), breeds (e.g. Yorkshire, Ashanti Black, Large White, Landrace) and their characteristics

subtopics.content: b. Importance of pig production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the importance to the economy i.e. source of employment, income, insulin used in pharmaceutical industries

subtopics.content: c. Systems of keeping pigs
subtopics.objective: Candidates should describe intensive, semi-intensive and extensive systems and their advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.content: d. Management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know management practices e.g. breeding, housing and feeding

subtopics.content: e. Slaughtering, processing and marketing of pigs
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know techniques of slaughtering, processing and marketing e.g. bacon making, quality control, packaging, storage, marketing outlets and advertisements

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance of pets
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the meaning of 'pet' (e.g. cat, dog, parrot) and the roles pets play e.g. security, income, shepherding, companionship

subtopics.content: b. Management of pets
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know housing, feeding, sanitation, breeding, grooming and care, pests and diseases and their control; and the importance of pet licencing and regular vaccination

subtopics.content: c. Training of pets
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know animal behaviour and reasons for training of pets

subtopics.content: d. Marketing of pets
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know marketing strategies and the value chain process in the marketing of pets

subtopics.content: a. Common breeds, distribution and characteristics
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know common breeds, their geographical distribution, distinguishing features between sheep and goats, and characteristics of breeds e.g. body size, hair cover and horn shape

subtopics.content: b. Importance of sheep and goats
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the social (e.g. religious), economic (income, hides and skin for leather) and nutritional (meat) importance, and production requirements using a value chain approach

subtopics.content: c. Management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know hoof trimming, housing, feeding, sanitation, disease and pest control, and determine age of sheep and goats by dentition

subtopics.content: d. Common parasites and diseases and their control
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know common parasites (ticks and worms) and diseases (e.g. anthrax, mastitis, foot rot), signs/symptoms and control measures

subtopics.content: e. Processing and marketing
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know techniques to ensure meat quality, safety and consumer satisfaction including slaughtering and processing, quality control, preservation and storage, packaging, advertising and marketing outlets

subtopics.content: a. Breeds and characteristics
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know common breeds of beef cattle in West Africa and Europe and their characteristics and general structure

subtopics.content: b. Importance of beef cattle production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the nutritional value of beef, use of hides, horns, bones and manure, and social and economic value of beef and live cattle

subtopics.content: c. Common production systems
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know systems e.g. extensive, pastoral, agro-pastoral, semi-intensive, intensive feedlot, pastures, their characteristics, strengths and weaknesses

subtopics.content: d. Planning, production and management of cattle for beef and traction
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the requirements (value chain approach), selection of management system, foundation stock, and qualities of bulls and cows selected for traction

subtopics.content: e. General management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should have skills in housing, feeding, breeding, fattening etc. and knowledge of training of yoked cattle

subtopics.content: f. Processing and marketing
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know techniques of slaughtering and processing of carcass, maintenance of safety standards, packaging and sale of meat products

subtopics.content: g. Major problems in beef cattle production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know negative effects of poor management on the environment, feed and water shortages, cattle theft, pests etc. and their solutions

subtopics.content: a. Breeds and features of dairy cow
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know examples of pure and cross bred dairy breeds in tropical and temperate regions and distinguishing features of a dairy cow

subtopics.content: b. Characteristics, sources and importance of milk
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know composition and nutritional value of fresh milk, sources of milk (goats, sheep, buffaloes, camels and cattle) and importance of milk including food, income, employment, trade

subtopics.content: c. Management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know requirements using a value chain approach e.g. market demand, inputs for wholesome milk, and selecting suitable breeds and management systems

subtopics.content: d. Diseases and their control
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know symptoms and methods of controlling mastitis, tuberculosis and ketosis

subtopics.content: e. Production, processing and marketing of milk and dairy products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know equipment for milking, milk handling and processing; pasteurization; products e.g. yoghurt, cottage cheese, tinned milk, powdered milk; consequences of consuming contaminated milk; quality and safety standards; packaging, storage and marketing

subtopics.content: f. Problems of dairy cattle production in warm climates
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know effects of warm climate on dairy animals and milk production and the solutions

sections.sectionTitle: Section I: Range and Pasture Management

subtopics.content: a. Basic terminologies in pasture and range management
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand terms e.g. pasture, pasture rotation, stocking rate, range, forage crops

subtopics.content: b. Types of pasture and their features
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know natural/range and artificial/cultivated pastures and their features

subtopics.content: c. Importance of pastures and forage crops in animal production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the role of forage and pasture crops in animal production

subtopics.content: d. Factors that affect the productivity of different types of pasture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know factors e.g. rainfall, soil fertility, temperature, weeds

subtopics.content: e. Major forage crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know common and scientific names of major forage crops and their classification

subtopics.content: f. Poisonous plants in pasture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know poisonous plants in pasture e.g. Lantana camara, Crotalaria rotundus

subtopics.content: a. Qualities of good pasture and forage species
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know qualities e.g. high productivity, palatability and fast growth

subtopics.content: b. Establishment of pasture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know cultural practices e.g. site selection, land preparation, methods of propagation (seeding, vegetative means), their merits and demerits

subtopics.content: c. Improving natural pastures
subtopics.objective: Candidates should understand the need and techniques for improving natural pastures

subtopics.content: d. Management of cultivated pastures
subtopics.objective: Candidates should have skills in managing cultivated pastures e.g. control of fire, proper stocking rate, disease prevention and control

subtopics.content: e. Harvesting of forage crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know tools/equipment for harvesting forage crops and yield determination

subtopics.content: a. Forage conservation and its importance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know forage conservation and its importance, forms of conserved forage (hay and silage), and differences between hay and silage based on physical, chemical and nutritive properties

subtopics.content: b. Preparation of hay and silage
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know processes and precautions e.g. cutting herbage at the right time, proper compacting, use of additives

subtopics.content: c. Utilization of crop residue in feeding animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know types of crop residue and merits and demerits of using residue for feeding ruminants

subtopics.content: a. Common breeds
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know common breeds of rabbits and grasscutter

subtopics.content: b. Importance of producing rabbits and grasscutters
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the importance e.g. source of meat, pelt, income

subtopics.content: c. Management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know housing, feeding, sanitation, breeding, disease and pest control and record keeping

subtopics.content: d. Processing and marketing
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know activities involved in processing and marketing of rabbits and grasscutter

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know the meaning and importance of snail farming

subtopics.content: b. External features of snails
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know external features of snails and their functions

subtopics.content: c. Types of species
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know types of species used for snail farming

subtopics.content: d. Site selection
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know factors to consider in site selection

subtopics.content: e. Management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know housing, feeding, sanitation, breeding, pest and disease control, record keeping, processing and marketing

subtopics.content: f. Processing and marketing of snails
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know steps involved in processing snails and marketing

subtopics.content: a. Establishing enterprises in animal husbandry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should know animal production enterprises, and factors to be considered and procedures in establishing an animal production enterprise

subtopics.content: 1. Breeds of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify common types and breeds of farm animals

subtopics.content: 2. Classification of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify farm animals based on type of digestive system i.e. ruminants, non-ruminant (monogastrics) and non-ruminant herbivores

topics.title: Anatomy and physiology of farm animals

subtopics.content: 3. Anatomy and physiology of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the orientation of external parts, draw and label animals and their parts, and identify and draw major anatomical structures in the various body systems, differences between the structures and their functions

subtopics.content: 4. Animal nutrition
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify common feedstuffs and supplements (e.g. maize, fish meal, oyster shell) and state the major nutrients; perform simple food tests for carbohydrates, fats and oils and protein; formulate feed using the Pearson Square Method, estimate cost of prepared feed and keep feed records; identify pests of stored feed and feedstuffs, their effects and control

topics.title: Main pests and parasites of farm animals

subtopics.content: 5. Main pests and parasites of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the main pests and parasites (ectoparasites and endoparasites), their effects and control, and draw and label the life cycles of tapeworm and roundworm

topics.title: Diseases of farm animals; their prevention and control

subtopics.content: 6. Diseases of farm animals; their prevention and control
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify main diseases and causal agents, and know simple preventive and control measures (drenching, dipping, spraying, vaccination) and the equipment and tools used

subtopics.content: 7. Artificial insemination
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the tools and equipment used in artificial insemination and their uses

subtopics.content: 8. Environmental physiology
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify and use equipment to determine parameters such as temperature, relative humidity, respiration rate and heart beat, and interpret the data

subtopics.content: 9. Management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify tools and equipment used for housing, breeding, brooding, feeding, identification, debeaking, castration, dehorning and candling, and their maintenance

subtopics.content: 10. Animal products and by-products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify animal products and by-products such as milk, skin, blood meal and feathers, and know their uses

subtopics.content: 11. Range and pasture management
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify forage crops (e.g. Panicum maximum), poisonous plants (e.g. Lantana camara), conserved forage (hay and silage), and tools and equipment used in cultivation and management of pastures and conservation of forage

subtopics.content: 12. Animal housing and structures
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify suitable materials for constructing animal houses and structures (e.g. cement, bamboo, wire mesh, wood) and appropriate structures for various farm animals (e.g. hutches for rabbits, open-sided houses for pigs)
